record.context_brief: Higher-dimensional Anderson model with Bernoulli disorder
record.original_question: For the discrete random Schrodinger operator in dimension d >= 2 with Bernoulli site variables omega_j taking the values +1 and -1 with equal probability, does the operator have purely singular spectrum?

evidence.quote: The same question is open if ωj = ±1 with equal probability.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\geq 2$ and consider the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^d)$. Define the discrete Anderson Hamiltonian
$$H_\omega = -\Delta + V_\omega,$$
where $\Delta$ is the standard discrete Laplacian on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, given by
$$(\Delta\psi)(j) = \sum_{|i-j|=1}\bigl(\psi(i)-\psi(j)\bigr),$$
and $V_\omega$ is the multiplication operator $(V_\omega\psi)(j)=\omega_j\,\psi(j)$, with $\{\omega_j\}_{j\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ an i.i.d. family of Bernoulli random variables satisfying
$$\mathbb{P}(\omega_j=+1)=\mathbb{P}(\omega_j=-1)=\tfrac{1}{2}.$$
Determine whether, almost surely with respect to the product Bernoulli measure, the spectrum of $H_\omega$ is purely singular (i.e., the absolutely continuous spectrum of $H_\omega$ is empty almost surely on the entire spectrum).
artifact.status_search_result: Localization (and hence pure point/singular spectrum) for the discrete Bernoulli Anderson model in dimensions d ≥ 2 throughout the spectrum remains an open problem. Partial results exist: localization is fully known in d=1, and in higher dimensions localization has been established only in the continuum Bernoulli–Anderson model near spectral edges (via quantitative unique continuation), or under additional assumptions. The discrete case with ±1 Bernoulli site potentials in d ≥ 2 is still not resolved as of recent work (e.g., 2025 alloy-type Bernoulli localization papers).

status_evidence.title: On localization for the alloy-type Anderson-Bernoulli model
status_evidence.snippet: Localization for multi-dimensional discrete Bernoulli–Anderson models is significantly challenging; results in higher dimensions have mostly been obtained in the continuum case near the bottom of the spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Discrete Bernoulli Anderson localization in d≥2 throughout the spectrum remains open.

status_evidence.title: The lattice Anderson model with discrete disorder (Imbrie)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishing localization in d≥2 for singular (e.g., Bernoulli) site distributions is a longstanding open problem; the Bernoulli case is the hardest.
status_evidence.claim: The Bernoulli case in d≥2 on the lattice is open.
